newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BRAVE ALBANIA GO DOWN TO KIRSTEN HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAVE ALBANIA GO DOWN TO KIRSTEN HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Substitute Ulf Kirsten scored a remarkable second half hat-trick as European champions Germany came back from a goal down to beat Albania 3-2 in a dramatic World Cup qualifying game on Wednesday.

Albania missed an early penalty, and then went ahead from a second spot kick in the 60th minute. Kirsten was brought on to turn the game round and struck three times before Albania's Bledar Kola scored another penalty in the last minute.
The game was played in Spain because of the current conflict in Albania, and a member of the country's Under-21 team said he and his team mates were hoping to be allowed to stay on in Spain.

Germany had started the game strongly, with Juergen Klinsmann and Stefan Reuter forcing fine saves out of Albanian keeper Foto Strakosha, who was again on form after a brilliant performance in Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Ukraine.

But the Germans were rocked by practically the Albanians' first break of the game when Altin Rraklel used his pace to break through the German defence only to be brought down as he bore down on goal by keeper Andreas Koepke.
Belgian referee Michel Piraux had no hesitation pointing to the spot, but failed to take any other action when a red card seemed the obvious next step.
The Albanians did not appeal for a card and failed to find compensation from the spot kick, which Koepke saved by diving to his right.
Klinsmann again went close before half-time and Dariusz Wosz headed wide when unmarked just after the break.

With Bayern Munich defender Christian Ziege creating constant danger down the left the Albanians were pushed backwards until the 60th minute when they broke down the left. Kola was sandwiched by two German defenders leading to a second penalty.
Kola took the kick himself and Koepke narrowly failed to save his second penalty of the evening.
Albania's lead lasted less than five minutes, as Kirsten, who had replaced Dieter Eilts, rose to head home a cross from the left.
A move from the left also led to Germany's second, when Kirsten rose at the far post and headed home a ball which somehow ended up in the back of the net despite Strakosha's efforts.
The third started on the same flank and ended in a simple tap-in for Kirsten's hat-trick.
In the 91st minute the Albanians hit back through yet another penalty, awarded after a mix-up in the area, but by then it was too late for them to find an equaliser.
"It is incredible that we should have won three penalties and scored two of them," Albanian coach Hafizi Astrit said. "I am happy with the match."
"We had to score quickly after their goal, but when we did it was almost logical that we would win as they lost speed and precision," Germany boss Berti Vogts said.

Albania - 1-Foto Strakosha, 2-Zamir Shduza (13-Arjon Bellai 68), 3-Ilir Shulku, 4-Eduard Abazi, 5-Rudi Vata, 6-Salvadorr Kacaj, 7-Atlin Haxih, 8-Aldan Bushi (18-Ervin Lance 90th), 9-Bledar Kola, 10-Altin Rraklel, 11-Igli Tare (14-Fatmir Vata 73)

Germany - 1-Andreas Koepke, 2-Stefan Reuter (16-Joerg Heinrich 58), 3-Christian Ziege, 4-Juergen Kohler, 5-Thomas Helmer, 6-Matthias Sammer, 7-Andreas Moeller, 8-Dieter Eilts (17-Ulf Kirsten 60), 9-Juergen Klinsmann, 10-Dariusz Wosz, 11-Oliver Bierhoff
